owner_and_source: California Department of Transportation (Caltrans), California Integrated Travel Program (Cal-ITP) -- 'Cal-ITP GTFS-Ingest Pipeline Dataset' on data.ca.gov (CKAN package cal-itp-gtfs-ingest-pipeline-dataset, id de6f1544-b162-4d16-997b-c183912c8e62), resource 0e4da89e-9330-43f8-8de9-305cb7d4918f. Cal-ITP fetches every California transit operator's GTFS nightly and concatenates one statewide CSV per GTFS table, preserving feed identity in a base64_url column. No API key, no registration, plain HTTPS.

geography: California, statewide -- every operator on Cal-ITP's nightly ingest list
time_coverage: current statewide snapshot; the assembly is refreshed and republished monthly (CKAN accrualPeriodicity R/P1M, metadata_modified 2026-07-21). Not a historical archive: one service-change generation, not a time series.
schema_and_format: CSV, 11 columns: base64_url, route_id, service_id, trip_id, trip_headsign, trip_short_name, direction_id, block_id, shape_id, wheelchair_accessible, bikes_allowed. THE REASON THIS PACKET EXISTS IS THE block_id COLUMN: it is the agency's own chained day of vehicle work, and consecutive trips sharing a block_id are the same physical vehicle. base64_url is the feed key -- trip_id is unique only WITHIN a feed, so every join must be on (base64_url, trip_id). block_id is optional in GTFS and is frequently blank; the emptiness rate is itself a finding, recorded in data/catalog/calitp-scheduled-deadhead.md.
update_frequency: monthly (CKAN accrualPeriodicity R/P1M). source_checksum is null -- trust-on-first-use, because the statewide assembly is rebuilt nightly and republished monthly, so no stable digest is publishable ahead of the pull. The digest actually retained is recorded in calitp-gtfs-trips.acquired.json.
canonical_contract: app.canonical.entities.Block and app.canonical.entities.DeadheadSegment (Program A, ADR-0047). trips.block_id maps to Block.block_ref and DeadheadSegment.block_ref; trips.service_id maps to Block.service_ref. Both are SOURCE refs and stay plain strings, exactly as those entities require -- they name an external agency's entities, never a Milexium aggregate.

quality_tests.name: header_carries_base64_url_and_block_id
quality_tests.description: the first line contains both base64_url (the feed key every join needs) and block_id (the field the whole packet depends on); without either the file is unusable for block chaining

quality_tests.name: trip_key_is_unique_per_feed
quality_tests.description: (base64_url, trip_id) is unique -- if it is not, the stop_times join would fan out and inflate every derived deadhead figure

acceptance_threshold: downloads over plain HTTPS with no credential, is CSV, > 10 MB, header contains base64_url, trip_id and block_id, and at least one row carries a non-empty block_id.
retention_and_deletion: retain. Small (~73 MB) and the single most load-bearing file in the packet -- it is the only place the block chaining lives. Reproducible monthly from the same URL; a fresher pull supersedes and the superseded object may be deleted once its acquired-record is superseded.
